themes.summary: Sources examine what students find useful or challenging in capstone projects.

themes.summary: Sources model competing objectives among students, faculty, and sponsors.

themes.summary: Sources consider engagement for historically underrepresented groups in IoT-based capstones.

themes.name: Course design models and capstone preparation
themes.summary: Sources describe course design approaches intended to prepare students for professional practice.

themes.name: Career information literacy
themes.summary: Sources compare student and employer emphases on career information literacy.

questions.question: How does scaffolded design thinking shape capstone engagement and teamwork?
What do students find valuable or challenging in project-based capstones?
How can conflicting incentives among students, faculty, and sponsors be modeled or managed?
How do IoT-based capstone projects affect engagement for historically underrepresented groups?
How do different capstone course designs prepare students for professional practice?
How do student and employer emphases on career information literacy align?

limitations: All selected records were screened from abstracts or publisher descriptions; full texts were not reviewed.
UC Library Search was used through the keyless Primo PNX REST fallback because no PRIMO_KEY was present.
The focused landscape and one component search identified capstone-specific literature, but coverage is not exhaustive.
Several useful sources were excluded as adjacent or duplicates during screening.
